Rashi on Megillah 21a:10:1.hebrew: הקורא עומד ויושב - אם רצה עומד, אם רצה יושב:
Rashi on Megillah 21a:10:1.english: One who reads [the Megillah], standing or sitting - If he wishes, [he reads] standing; if he wishes, [he reads] sitting:

Rashi on Megillah 21a:10:2.hebrew: קראוה שנים - יחד, יצאו, ולא אמרינן "אין שני קולות נשמעין כאחד":
Rashi on Megillah 21a:10:2.english: [If] two people read it - together, they have fulfilled [their obligation], and we do not say [that] two voices cannot be heard as one:

Rashi on Megillah 21a:10:3.english: One should not recite a blessing - He does not need to recite a blessing.

Rashi on Megillah 21a:11:1.hebrew: בשני ובחמישי בשבת ובשבת במנחה - עזרא תיקן שיהו קורין בשני ובחמישי, בבבא קמא בפרק מרובה (בבא קמא דף פב.), והכא אשמעינן דשלשה הן: כהן ולוי וישראל:
Rashi on Megillah 21a:11:1.english: On Mondays and Thursdays, [and] on Shabbat during the afternoon service - Ezra instituted that they should read [from the Torah] on Mondays and Thursdays, [as stated] in Bava Kamma in the chapter [entitled] Merubah (Bava Kamma 82a); and here [the Mishnah] teaches us that they are three [readers]: a Kohen, a Levite, and an Israelite.

Rashi on Megillah 21a:11:2.hebrew: ואין מוסיפין עליהן - שלא יקשה לצבור, מפני שהן ימי מלאכה, ושבת במנחה סמוך לחשיכה הוא, שהרי כל היום היו רגילין לדרוש:
Rashi on Megillah 21a:11:2.english: And one may not add to them - So that it will not be burdensome for the congregation, because they [Mondays and Thursdays] are workdays, and Shabbat afternoon is close to dark, for all day they were accustomed to expound:

Rashi on Megillah 21a:11:3.english: And one does not conclude [with a reading from the Prophets] - because of this very reason [so as not to burden the congregation].

Rashi on Megillah 21a:11:4.english: The one who begins and the one who concludes - In the Gemara [it] explains [this]:

Rashi on Megillah 21a:12:1.hebrew: ואין מוסיפין עליהן - בראשי חדשים וחול המועד נמי איכא ביטול מלאכה, דמלאכת דבר האבד מותרת:
Rashi on Megillah 21a:12:1.english: Nor add to them - [On] Rosh Chodesh and Chol HaMoed as well there is interruption of work, since work [to prevent] a loss is permitted:

Rashi on Megillah 21a:14:1.english: Which is not the case with the Torah - For one does not read the Torah in public while sitting:

Rashi on Megillah 21a:14:2.english: As it were - [This expression] is said regarding the Holy One, Blessed be He, as [regarding] a human being of whom such [a thing] can be said:

Rashi on Megillah 21a:15:1.hebrew: שלא ישב על גבי המטה - אלא או שניהם על גבי המטה, או שניהם על גבי קרקע:
Rashi on Megillah 21a:15:1.english: That [the teacher] should not sit on a couch - Rather, either both of them [should sit] on a couch, or both of them [should sit] on the ground:

Rashi on Megillah 21a:17:1.english: And learns - from the mouth of the Almighty:

Rashi on Megillah 21a:17:2.english: Sitting and reviewing - [repeating] a second time by himself what he had learned:

Rashi on Megillah 21a:17:3.english: Easy [matters] - Soft and easy matters that a person is quick to understand:

Rashi on Megillah 21a:1:1.hebrew: משפט ביום - דכתיב "והיה ביום הנחילו את בניו" (דברים כ״א:ט״ז), אורעה כל הפרשה כולה להיות דין, במס' סנהדרין בפ' אחד דיני ממונות (סנהדרין דף לד:):
Rashi on Megillah 21a:1:1.english: Judgment [is conducted] by day - As it is written, "And it shall be, on the day that he bequeaths to his sons" (Deuteronomy 21:16), [whereby] the entire section was established to be [a matter of] judgment, in tractate Sanhedrin, in the chapter [entitled] Echad Dinei Mamonot (Sanhedrin 34b):

Rashi on Megillah 21a:2:1.english: For the purification of a leper - [This refers to the purification performed] with birds, cedar wood, hyssop, and crimson thread.

Rashi on Megillah 21a:3:1.hebrew: דאמר מר קצירה וספירת בלילה - ויליף לה במס' מנחות מקראי:
Rashi on Megillah 21a:3:1.english: As the Master said: Reaping and counting [are performed] at night - And [the Gemara] derives this in Tractate Menachot from verses:

Rashi on Megillah 21a:3:2.english: All night until the morning - [That is, as the verse states:] “upon the hearth upon the altar all night until the morning.”

Rashi on Megillah 21a:5:1.hebrew: וכר' יוסי - דאמר במסכת מנחות: אפילו סילק את הישנה שחרית וסידר את החדשה ערבית — אף זו היתה תמיד, ומהו "תמיד"? שלא ילין שולחן בלא לחם. אבל לרבנן, טפחו של זה מסדר בצד טפחו של מסלק:
Rashi on Megillah 21a:5:1.english: And [in accordance with] Rabbi Yosei - who said in Tractate Menachot: Even if one removed the old [showbread] in the morning and arranged the new [showbread] in the evening, even this was [considered] "continually." And what is [the meaning of] "continually"? That the Table should not remain overnight without bread. But according to the Rabbis, the handbreadth of this one arranging is alongside the handbreadth of the one removing:

Tosafot on Megillah 21a:10:1.hebrew: הקורא. ואין מפטירין בנביא. - קשיא לר"ת, דהא בפרק במה מדליקין (שבת דף כד. ושם) אמר רב אחדבוי שאלמלא שבת אין נביא במנחה ביום טוב שחל להיות בשבת. וצריך לומר דהאי דקאמר התם דמפטיר בנביא במנחה בשבת כשחל ביו"ט — לאו דוקא נביא, אלא רוצה לומר בכתובים, כדאמרינן פרק כל כתבי (שבת קטז:): בנהרדעא פסקי סדרא בכתובים במנחה בשבתא, ופסקי היינו הפטרה, ומקומות יש שנוהגין לעשות כן. והטעם שמפטיר במנחה בתענית ולא בשחרית, משום דכתיב בה: "שמרו משפט ועשו צדקה" (ישעיהו נו), ואגרא דתעניתא צדקתא לעת ערב, ומש"ה נכון לאומרו בערב אחר שעשו צדקה:
Tosafot on Megillah 21a:10:1.english: One who reads. And one does not conclude with [a reading from] the Prophets. - This is difficult for Rabbeinu Tam, for in the chapter [entitled] Bameh Madlikin (Shabbat 24a, and there [in the commentary]), Rav Aḥadvoi said that were it not for Shabbat, there is no [reading from] the Prophets at Minḥa on a Festival that falls on Shabbat [implying that when it does fall on Shabbat, one does read from the Prophets at Minḥa]. And one must say that that which he said there — that one concludes with [a reading from] the Prophets at Minḥa on Shabbat when a Festival falls [on it] — does not mean literally the Prophets; rather, he means [a reading] from the Writings, as we say in the chapter [entitled] Kol Kitvei (Shabbat 116b): "In Nehardea they read a section from the Writings at Minḥa on Shabbat," and "they read a section" means a haftara, and there are places where it is customary to do so. And the reason that one concludes with [a haftara] at Minḥa on a fast day and not at Shaḥarit is because it is written in it: "Keep justice and do righteousness" (Isaiah 56[:1]), and the reward of a fast is charity [given] toward evening; and therefore it is proper to recite it in the evening after they have given charity:

Tosafot on Megillah 21a:11:1.hebrew: הקורא. ואין מפטירין בנביא - קשיא לר"ת, דהא בפרק במה מדליקין (שבת דף כד.ושם) אמר רב אחדבוי: שאלמלא שבת, אין נביא במנחה ביום טוב שחל להיות בשבת! וצריך לומר דהאי דקאמר התם דמפטיר בנביא במנחה בשבת כשחל ביו"ט, לאו דוקא נביא, אלא רוצה לומר בכתובים, כדאמרינן פרק כל כתבי (שבת קטו:): בנהרדעא פסקי סדרא בכתובים במנחה בשבתא; ופסקי היינו הפטרה, ומקומות יש שנוהגין לעשות כן. והטעם שמפטיר במנחה בתענית ולא בשחרית, משום דכתיב בה "שמרו משפט ועשו צדקה" (ישעיה נו), ואגרא דתעניתא צדקתא לעת ערב, ומש"ה נכון לאומרו בערב, אחר שעשו צדקה:
Tosafot on Megillah 21a:11:1.english: Hakore. And one does not conclude with [a reading from] the Prophets - This is difficult for Rabbeinu Tam, for in the chapter [entitled] Bameh Madlikin (Shabbat 24a, and there), Rav Aḥadvoi said: "Were it not for Shabbat, there is no [reading from] the Prophets at Minḥa on a Festival that falls on Shabbat!" And one must say that when [the Gemara] says there that one concludes with [a reading from] the Prophets at Minḥa on Shabbat when it falls on a Festival, it does not literally mean the Prophets, rather it means [a reading] from the Writings, as we say in the chapter [entitled] Kol Kitvei (Shabbat 115b): "In Nehardea they would read a section from the Writings at Minḥa on Shabbat"; and "reading a section" [paskei] means haftarah, and there are places that have the custom to do so. And the reason that one concludes with a haftarah at Minḥa on a fast day and not at Shaḥarit is because it is written in it: "Observe justice and do righteousness [tzedakah]" (Isaiah 56[:1]), and the reward of a fast is charity [tzedakta] toward evening; therefore, it is proper to recite it in the evening, after they have performed charity:

Tosafot on Megillah 21a:11:2.hebrew: הפותח והחותם בתורה מברך לפניה ולאחריה - קשיא: אמאי תנא הך מילתא הכא ג' פעמים, דהא בחד זימנא סגיא? וי"ל, דהוה סלקא דעתך דכל דטפי מילתא מחבריה מברך לפניה ולאחריה; מש"ה אצטריך למתני בכולהו:
Tosafot on Megillah 21a:11:2.english: The one who begins and the one who concludes [the reading from] the Torah recite a blessing before it and after it - It is difficult: why did [the Tanna] teach this matter here three times, since one time would suffice? And one can answer that you might have thought that [in] any [case] that is greater than its fellow, one recites a blessing before it and after it; therefore, it was necessary to teach [it] in all of them:

Tosafot on Megillah 21a:14:1.hebrew: אלמלא מקרא כתוב - קשיא, שיש "אלמלא" שרוצה לומר "אילו לא", כגון הכא, וכגון "אלמלא אגרות הראשונות" (לעיל מגילה דף יב:), וכן הרבה; ויש "אלמלא" שרוצה לומר "אילו היה", כגון "אלמלא נגדוה לחנניה מישאל ועזריה" (כתובות דף לג:), וכן "אלמלא לוי אתה" וכו' (לקמן מגילה דף כד:), ומאי שנא? ואומר ר"ת, דהיכא שיש אל"ף בסוף, "אלמלא", רוצה לומר "אילו לא"; והיכא דכתי' "אלמלי" ביו"ד, רוצה לומר "אילו היה":
Tosafot on Megillah 21a:14:1.english: Were the verse not written - This is difficult: for there is [a usage of] "ilmalei" that means "if not," such as here, and such as "Were it not for the first letters" (above, Megillah 12b), and likewise many [others]; and there is [a usage of] "ilmalei" that means "if it were," [such as] "Had they lashed Ḥananyah, Mishael, and Azaryah" (Ketubot 33b), and likewise "Were you a Levite," etc. (below, Megillah 24b) — so what is the difference? And Rabbeinu Tam says that wherever there is an alef at the end — "אלמלא" — it means "if not"; and wherever it is written "אלמלי" with a yod, it means "if it were":

Tosafot on Megillah 21a:3:1.hebrew: ולהקטר חלבים כל הלילה עד הבוקר - והיינו דוקא שנתעכלו האברים קודם חצות, ששלטה בהן האור; אבל אם לא משלה בהן, אין נמשכין אחר חצות, כדאמר ר' יוחנן סוף פ"ק דיומא (דף כ:):
Tosafot on Megillah 21a:3:1.english: And for burning the fats... “all night until the morning” - And this is specifically [when] the limbs were [partially] consumed before midnight, [i.e.,] that the fire had taken hold of them; but if [the fire] had not taken hold of them, they do not continue [to be burned] after midnight, as Rabbi Yoḥanan says at the end of the first chapter of Yoma (20b):

Tosafot on Megillah 21a:8:1.hebrew: לאתויי אכילת פסחים ודלא כרבי אלעזר ב"ע - מ"מ נראה דהלכה כר' אלעזר, דהא איכא סתמא בערבי פסחים (פסחים קכ: ושם) דקאי כוותיה, דתנן: הפסח אחר חצות מטמא את הידים. וכן משנה באיזהו מקומן (זבחים דף נו:), וסתמא בסוף פ"ק דברכות (דף ט.) גבי מעשה ובאו בניו של רבן גמליאל מבית המשתה וכו', אמר להם: כל מה שאמרו חכמים "עד חצות", מצותן עד שיעלה עמוד השחר, ואילו אכילת פסחים לא קתני, ומוקי לה כראב"ע דאמר עד חצות. וא"כ צריך למהר לאכול מצה בלילי פסחים קודם חצות, ואפילו מצה של אפיקומן, שהרי חיוב מצה בזמן הזה הוה דאורייתא; אבל בהלל של אחר אפיקומן אין להחמיר כל כך, שהרי מדרבנן הוא:
Tosafot on Megillah 21a:8:1.english: To include the eating of the Paschal offerings, and [this is] not in accordance with Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya - Nevertheless, it appears that the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Elazar [ben Azarya], for there is an anonymous [mishna] in [the chapter entitled] Arvei Pesachim (Pesachim 120b and there) that stands in accordance with him, as we learned [in a mishna]: "The Paschal offering after midnight renders the hands impure." And similarly [there is] a mishna in [the chapter entitled] Eizehu Mekoman (Zevachim 56b), and an anonymous [mishna] at the end of the first chapter of Berakhot (9a) regarding the incident [where] the sons of Rabban Gamliel came from a banquet hall, etc. — he said to them: "All those [mitzvot] regarding which the Sages said 'until midnight,' their mitzva [remains] until the break of dawn"; yet [the Gemara there] does not teach the eating of the Paschal offerings, and establishes [that mishna] in accordance with Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya, who says [it is eaten only] until midnight. And if so, one must hasten to eat matza on the nights of Passover before midnight, and even the matza of the afikoman, since the obligation of matza in this era is Torah law; however, regarding the Hallel after the afikoman, one need not be so stringent, since it is rabbinic:
